_comment: THE ROUTE TABLE THIS APPLICATION SERVES, WRITTEN DOWN SO A MOVE OR A RENAME
tools/verify-boot.js assembles the real application and compares what it
actually exposes against this list, in BOTH directions: a route that went
missing fails, and so does one that appeared. The second half matters as
much as the first - nothing says 'a module was registered twice', 'a path
drifted by a character' or 'somebody added a route without saying so' as
TWO ENTRIES ARE NOT LITERAL PATHS AND ARE LISTED SEPARATELY BELOW. The
legal shell answers a REGEX rather than a literal path, and the health

non_literal.GET /legal/<policy>.html: a regex route in modules/legal, answering six URLs from one template. Its six concrete paths are asserted by test/browser/journeys.spec.js, and listed in core/config/static-mounts.js as ROUTED_URLS so tools/verify-links.js knows they are real.
